t:
(a) Report.—Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Energy, and the Director of National Intelligence, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report on Cooperative Threat Reduction Programs in the Russian Federation. 
    (b) Matters Included.—The report under subsection (a) shall include the following:
        (1) Identification of nonproliferation programs in Russia that—
            (A) have accomplished their long-term objectives in reducing the threat of proliferation of weapons of mass destruction; and 
            (B) will be phased out during the five-year period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act.  
        (2) Identification of—
            (A) nonproliferation programs in Russia that—
                (i) reduce the threat of the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction; and 
                (ii) will not be phased out during such five-year period; and  
            (B) the metrics to evaluate the success of such programs.  
        (3) Identification of—
            (A) the nature of the threat of the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction that underpin the programs described in paragraphs (1) and (2); and 
            (B) the current and foreseeable threats that are addressed by such programs.  
        (4) The impact on nonproliferation programs in Russia and the risks and benefits to national security if the current agreement regarding such programs (commonly referred to as the “umbrella agreement”) is amended or not renewed. 
        (5) What steps, if any, will be taken to continue or terminate ongoing nonproliferation programs if the umbrella agreement is not renewed.  
    (c) Form.—The report under subsection (a) shall be in unclassified form, but may contain a classified annex. 
    (d) Appropriate Congressional Committees Defined.—In this section, the term “appropriate congressional committees” means—
        (1) the Committee on Armed Services and the Committee on Foreign Affairs of the House of Representatives; and 
        (2) the Committee on Armed Services and the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate.

fable.w: The tempting reading treats the "coordination" language and the reference to the "umbrella agreement" as participation. But the coordination is solely among federal officials (Defense, State, Energy, DNI), and the report goes to congressional committees, all inside the federal government. The umbrella agreement is only mentioned as a topic of the report, with no process that brings states, the public, experts, or other outside parties into a federal decision.
fable.s: the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Energy, and the Director of National Intelligence, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report

qwen_block.w: The section requires federal officials (Secretaries and the Director of National Intelligence) to coordinate with each other, which is intra-governmental coordination. It then requires them to submit a report to Congress, which is also inside the federal government. There is no consultation or coordination with parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public) before a decision is made.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Energy, and the Director of National Intelligence, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report

opus.w: The only coordination is among federal officials (the Secretaries of Defense, State and Energy, and the Director of National Intelligence), and the report goes to congressional committees. Both of these stay inside the federal government. The reference to the umbrella agreement with Russia is just a topic the report must cover; it creates no process for outside parties to consult on, comment on, or challenge a federal decision. Although the language sounds procedural, no one outside the federal government takes part.
opus.s: the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Energy, and the Director of National Intelligence, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report on Cooperative Threat Reduction Programs in the Russian Federation.
opus.b:
This section does not involve participation.

1. **The tempting reading:** The section says the Secretary of Defense acts "in coordination with" other officials. It also sends a report to congressional committees and mentions an "umbrella agreement" with Russia. All of this sounds procedural, but none of it crosses the federal boundary.
   - Everyone the Secretary coordinates with is a federal official.
   - The report goes to Congress, which is inside the federal government.
   - The umbrella agreement only appears as something the report must analyze. No outside party gets a role in a federal decision.

2. **Label:**

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense to coordinate with other federal officials (Secretaries of State and Energy, Director of National Intelligence) and submit a report to Congress. All these actors are inside the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes intra-governmental coordination and reports to Congress as participation. There is no consultation or coordination with entities outside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Energy, and the Director of National Intelligence, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "coordination" with other Secretaries implies participation. However, the Secretaries of State, Energy, and the Director of National Intelligence are all federal officials inside the government. Coordination between federal agencies is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. Furthermore, the report is submitted to Congress, which is also inside the federal government. There is no involvement of outside parties (states, tribes, public, experts, etc.) in the decision-making process described here.
